findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (including the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet) are stored without an enforced server-side encryption policy.

The bucket declares no ACL, no bucket policy, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so it relies entirely on account defaults; a later object ACL or bucket policy change could expose the archived reports and vendor roster publicly.
No logging block is configured, so read and write access to the archived reports and the vendor roster object is not recorded, undermining detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed irrecoverably, including by an actor seeking to remove evidence.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without an enforced encryption policy.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding ledger exports, so there is no audit trail of read or write access to financial data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket; the private canned ACL alone does not prevent a later bucket policy or object ACL from exposing ledger data publicly.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, allowing silent overwrite or deletion of ledger export objects with no recovery path.
The model artifacts bucket configures versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so proprietary model data is stored without an enforced encryption policy.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, so only the private ACL protects the bucket; a future policy or ACL change could expose model artifacts.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks commonly contain internal hostnames, procedures and occasionally credentials, and are stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not audited.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, leaving it dependent on account defaults to remain private.

The ACL is set to the malformed value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" rather than the valid canned ACL "log-delivery-write", so the intended log-delivery grant is not applied and the audit log bucket's access control is left in an unintended state.
The central audit/log-delivery bucket sets force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete, so audit logs can be deleted wholesale, undermining the tamper-resistance of the audit trail.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is applied to the bucket receiving access logs for model_artifacts, so audit data could be exposed by a subsequent policy or ACL change.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact and business data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption, so the object is stored unencrypted.
